context: A uni student interviews a retired baseball player
purpose: Teach: バトン/選手権/投手/巨人/クロアチア/アルゼンチン/カリフォルニア/大地

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間ありがとうございます。早速ですが、高校時代の選手権大会の思い出を教えていただけますか？
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. To start, could you tell me your memories of the high school championship?
lines.style: Polite interview opening, formal university-student tone with respectful curiosity.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、あの夏のことはよう覚えとるよ。私は先発投手でね、決勝でマウンドに立ったんだ。
lines.en: Ah, I remember that summer well. I was the starting pitcher, and stood on the mound in the final.
lines.style: Warm elder reminiscence, slightly old-fashioned masculine speech with nostalgic pride.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: すごいですね。その後プロ入りされて、巨人軍で長く活躍されたと伺いました。
lines.en: That's amazing. I heard that afterwards you went pro and played for the Giants for many years.
lines.style: Impressed follow-up question, respectful interviewer building rapport gradually.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうそう。引退してからは国際大会のコーチもやってね、クロアチア代表やアルゼンチン代表とも試合したよ。
lines.en: That's right. After retiring, I coached for international tournaments, even facing Croatia and Argentina.
lines.style: Conversational storytelling, elder sharing varied career experiences with casual ease.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 海外でも指導されていたんですね。確かカリフォルニア州でも教えていらっしゃったとか？
lines.en: So you taught overseas as well. I believe you also coached in California, is that right?
lines.style: Curious clarifying question, showing the student has done his homework respectfully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: よく調べたねえ。あそこは大地が広くて、若い選手もみんなのびのびしとった。
lines.en: You really did your research. The land there is vast, and the young players were so carefree.
lines.style: Praising the student warmly, elder reflecting on landscape with poetic appreciation.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 最後に、これからの若い選手たちにバトンを渡す立場として、何かメッセージはありますか？
lines.en: Finally, as someone passing the baton to the next generation, do you have any message?
lines.style: Reflective closing question, formal university-student metaphor used thoughtfully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 失敗を恐れず、自分の足でしっかり大地を踏みしめて進んでほしい。それだけだよ。
lines.en: Don't fear failure, and walk forward planting your own feet firmly on the earth. That's all.
lines.style: Heartfelt closing wisdom, elder offering simple grounded advice with sincerity.
